_about: Public-domain John Lingard (1771-1851), English Catholic priest and historian, for the Word Hoard: his church writings, The Antiquities of the Anglo-Saxon Church (second edition, 1810), the History and Antiquities of the Anglo-Saxon Church (1845, two volumes), his Collection of Tracts (1826), Catechistical Instructions (1841), A Review of Certain Anti-Catholic Publications (1813) and Strictures on Dr. Marsh's Comparative View (1815), from Internet Archive scans. His History of England is listed as an alternate, not shelved. Added 2026-10-18 by lane A, round 35 (my pick); Adam may veto the whole shelf. Every printing dated before 1930, so public domain in the US. No uids minted.

lingard-antiquities-1810: The Antiquities of the Anglo-Saxon Church, second edition (Newcastle: Edward Walker; sold by J. Booker and Keating, London, 1810)
lingard-history-antiquities-1: The History and Antiquities of the Anglo-Saxon Church, vol. I (London: C. Dolman, 1845)
lingard-history-antiquities-2: The History and Antiquities of the Anglo-Saxon Church, vol. II (London: C. Dolman, 1845)
lingard-collection-tracts: A Collection of Tracts on Several Subjects connected with the Civil and Religious Principles of Catholics (London: Keating and Brown, 1826)
lingard-catechistical-instructions: Catechistical Instructions on the Doctrines and Worship of the Catholic Church, second edition, revised and corrected (New York: Patrick S. Casserly & Sons, 1841)
lingard-review-anti-catholic: A Review of Certain Anti-Catholic Publications (London: Joseph Booker, 1813)
lingard-strictures-marsh: Strictures on Dr. Marsh's Comparative View of the Churches of England and Rome (London: Joseph Booker, 1815)

_alternates.lingard-history-england: The History of England, first edition (London: J. Mawman, then Baldwin and Cradock, 1819-1830, eight volumes; vols IV-VIII catalogued 1819 in error), later sets of 1825 and 1837, and the 1912 Belloc edition (PG 10700)
_alternates.lingard-copies: Other Antiquities copies (1810 BSB, Philadelphia 1841, Baltimore 1851-54) and the 1858 History and Antiquities

_excluded.lingard-anonymous: A New Version of the Four Gospels (1836, 'by a Catholic') and two controversial pamphlets: their title pages name no one; Ward's Errata; the timber treatise by another John Lingard

lingard-collection-tracts.author: title page read: 'By the Rev. J. Lingard, D.D.' (OCR 'tLINGARD')
